newsitem.title: UK: "Grey man" Major named BBC personality of year.
newsitem.headline: "Grey man" Major named BBC personality of year.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major, often derided as the grey man of British politics, was named on Thursday as personality of the year by BBC radio's flagship current affairs programme.
Major won 23 percent of votes in the "Today" programme's annual poll of listeners. In second place was a young nursery school nurse who defended her infants from a machete attack.

A total of 140,000 votes was cast in the final round of the poll, which was mired in controversy this year after Tony Blair, leader of the opposition Labour party, was disqualified after a party official asked supporters to vote for him.
In another sign of how seriously some people take the poll, the BBC said it deducted 4,000 votes from Major's total after it detected some listeners had cast multiple votes in his favour.
"However suspect the poll, we hope that this will give John Major the confidence to call a general election so the people can decide who should be running the country," a Labour spokesman said.
Major, whose party trails badly in the opinion polls, must call the election by May 22.
